Subject: Dedicated capacity — post-demo recap, isolation & scaling plan

Hi Melissa / Rajiv —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture the key pain points, the proposal-level sizing, and clear next steps so your procurement and security teams can move quickly if this looks aligned. Short version up top, details below.

TL;DR
- Main asks: Dedicated GPU pool with VPC isolation, customer-managed keys, predictable baseline throughput, and a canary rollout approach for patient-facing models.
- Proposed baseline: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with autoscale to 8 GPUs for peak windows.
- SLA targets discussed: 99.9% uptime; P95 generation latency target ~120ms, P99 budgeted at <= 350ms for 2k-token prompts; embedding queries target P99 <= 200ms.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Latency sensitivity: triage and automated chart summarization need sub-200ms p99 for embeddings to keep UI snappy during concurrent clinician sessions.
- Data residency & isolation: logs and inference telemetry must remain inside your VPC; ability to use customer KMS for model I/O keys.
- Predictable cost & capacity: you want a reserved baseline for weekdays with burst capacity on demand; procurement prefers a 12-month committed pool.
- Safe rollout: legal and clinical risk teams want canary traffic routing, canary data retention controls, and a rollback path.

Proposal (high level)
- Dedicated Reserved: 4x reserved GPUs attached to a private VPC endpoint; burst pool up to +4 GPUs via autoscale.
- Networking: Private peering with option for strict egress rules; we can support static IPs for allowlists and provide a network sketch (attached).
- Security: Customer KMS support, audit log exports to your SIEM, SOC2 report available; will start the security questionnaire exchange next.
- Operations: Canary rollout plan (10% traffic for 48h -> 50% for 24h -> full), automatic fallback to smaller model family in case of latency/throughput regressions.

Next steps / asks (proposed dates)
1) I'll share a sizing/proposal PDF (attached) and a short network sketch — please confirm if 4x reserved GPUs + burst to 8 looks right (by Fri 2/20).
2) Melissa/Rajiv: please loop in your procurement and IT security and share a point of contact for the security questionnaire (ideally by Mon 2/22).
3) Dev / Laura: I'll need a short canary/runbook draft and a proposed calendar for a pilot in staging (target week of 3/8).
4) Legal: once procurement gives timing, we'll provide contract redlines and an expected lead time for capacity (typical lead ~2–4 weeks after PO).

Attachments: MediEast-Dedicated-Proposal-v1.pdf (proposal + cost model), medieast-network-sketch.png (network peering & firewall notes).

If anything above is off, tell me and I’ll adjust. Otherwise, happy to jump on a 30m sync with procurement/security this week.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Appreciate the thorough recap and the proposal PDF. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Confirming peak concurrent embedding QPS: we expect short-term peak ~1,200 qps (concurrent clinician sessions across regions), average ~350 qps.
- Retention & logging: retention windows for inference logs should be configurable; for production we want 90-day rolling retention in our SIEM.
- Compliance docs: please share SOC 2 and the most recent pen test summary.
- Canary: yes — 10% for 48 hours then expand sounds good, but our clinical ops needs an explicit rollback runbook (who triggers, what metrics).
- Procurement timing: we can aim to get you a PO in early March if pricing and contract terms are within our procurement thresholds.

Two asks: 1) Can you route the security questionnaire to it-security@medieast.com and 2) can your SRE/solutions engineer join a 45m call next Tue 2/24 at 10:00 PT to go over network and canary details?

Thanks —
Melissa Hart
Director, Digital Services | MediEast Health

Karthik / team —

Thanks — a couple of technical clarifications I recommend we include in the pilot doc to reduce surprise during the staging run:

- KV cache + batching: For summarization flows we recommend enabling per-session KV caching and session affinity so clinicians hitting the same patient context get the cached KV for latency reduction. This changes memory footprint: plan for an extra ~18–22GB per GPU depending on sequence lengths.
- Model variants: We will propose 1 production model (quantized fp16) + a smaller fallback model for extreme load to keep p95 bounded. Behavioral differences will be documented in the eval appendix.
- Canary metrics: p95 latency, p99 latency, error-rate (5xx), token cost delta > 15% and user-facing error incidents (tracked via a shared Slack channel).
- Networking: we can provide a VPN peering option or static egress IPs; static IPs will simplify your firewall allow-lists.

I will draft a 1-page runbook and a resource sizing table (GPU memory, expected token throughput, autoscale thresholds) and share by Mon 2/22. Laura, can you add the deployment rollback steps and runbook ownership?

- Dev
